messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@biocorp.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@biocorp.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Sealed-environment qualification + risk heatmap (post-call)

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard
- Primary objective: run sensitive R&D workloads in an air-gapped/private deployment (no egress from the appliance).
- Latency SLO: median < 30 ms token latency for retrieval-heavy prompts; bursts up to 250 qps expected for batch scoring windows.
- Maintenance constraints: monthly 4-hour maintenance window (local IT), on-site spares preferred, firmware/patching must be auditable and deliverable offline.
- Compliance: KMS/HSM integration and export-controlled data classification.

Open decisions we need to qualify
1) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: you indicated Private (air-gapped) is the preferred baseline but want confirmation on maintenance model and upgrade cadence.
2) Hardware sizing vs spares: need to confirm whether local spares are acceptable or we must ship replacement units.
3) Model update path: confirm if signed model artifacts delivered via USB/media is acceptable.

Attached I dropped our private-deploy qualifier (redwood_private_qualifier_v2.pdf) and a template for recording site constraints (biocorp_hw_constraints.xlsx). Please fill the hw constraints sheet and return it — that will let Karthik and the engineering team size the BOM.

Next steps / owners
- Aisha: confirm procurement lead (Samir) and complete hw_constraints.xlsx by EOD Wed (2026-11-03).
- Priya: initiate NDA and procurement intake; draft PO path.
- Karthik: produce initial BOM + offline upgrade playbook once hw sheet is returned.
- Ben: schedule on-site survey (or remote site walk) — propose week of Nov 9.

High-level timeline (tentative)
- Qualifier returned -> 3 business days -> BOM draft
- BOM agreed + PO issued -> 4–6 weeks -> hardware procurement and staging
- Staging -> on-site install and validation -> 1 week (canary followed by full ramp)

If any of the above assumptions are off, call it out — I want to avoid surprises around maintenance and model updates.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: redwood_private_qualifier_v2.pdf (form), biocorp_hw_constraints.xlsx (template)

Ben —

Appreciate the recap and clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: Samir is the right procurement lead. I've CC'd him.
- Model updates: We cannot accept inbound internet pulls. Signed model artifacts delivered via encrypted external media + HSM verification on the appliance is our preference. Can you confirm Redwood supports signed-offline model images and a verification stub?
- Spare parts: we prefer to keep 1 GPU node spare on-site for critical deployments. Do you support shipping spares or should we include that in our procurement?
- Patching cadence: monthly non-critical patches, quarterly security-only patches with an auditable change log.

We will review the HW sheet and aim to return it by 2026-11-03 but Samir may need internal approvals which could slip.

Also, can you provide a short summary of the differences in operational cost and SLA between Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (appliance) — high-level ballpark figures only, we just need something for procurement to compare.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Infrastructure Security | BioCorps Labs
aisha.khan@biocorp.com

Attachment: site-security-checklist.pdf (I attached a short internal checklist that highlights our encryption and network isolation constraints)

Hi all —

Quick technical response and what I'll deliver after I get the completed hw_constraints.xlsx: 

Hardware recommendations (initial)
- 2x inference nodes (A100-equivalent) per appliance for redundancy; 1x spare GPU node on-site (customer-owned or Redwood-managed).
- NVMe: RAID1 for model store; capacity depends on model family (gpt-like 13B quantized ~12–18GB, 70B quantized ~60–80GB).
- Local KMS/HSM: we support PKCS#11-compatible HSMs; offline key injection is supported.

Offline upgrades and patches
- Model/artifact delivery: signed tarball with SHA256 + Redwood signature; appliance verifies signature using customer-supplied public key (HSM).
- Firmware/OS patches: delivered as signed bundles; we support orchestrated offline patch application during your maintenance window.
- Patch cadence: we can support monthly non-critical and quarterly security-only as requested; emergency rolling updates are handled via signed emergency bundles and manual approval.

Support & spares
- SLA: 24x7 remote support; hardware RMA options: same-day swap if Redwood-managed spares contract is purchased; otherwise next-business-day replacement shipment.

Deliverables (Karthik) — scheduled after hw sheet is returned:
1) hardware-bom-draft.csv (draft)
2) offline-patch-playbook.docx (MOP draft)
3) risk_heatmap.pdf (technical risk + mitigations)

If anything in the above conflicts with your procurement constraints please flag it. I'll start drafting the BOM today and drop the files to the shared Drive link in this thread.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: hardware-bom-draft.csv, offline-patch-playbook.docx
